all: Give every controlled device a DHCP reservation (or static IP outside the pool) before adding it in Composer.
Wire it if it has an Ethernet port. Several TVs only wake over LAN (Wake-on-LAN) when wired.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on TVs, AVRs and sources unless the driver needs it. CEC fights the control system (inputs and power changing on their own).
Set network/IP standby to the 'always on' option so the device can be turned on over IP. It uses a little more standby power.
Turn off eco / auto power off / auto standby timers so devices don't sleep or drop off the network behind Control4's back.
Turn on Control4 SDDP where the device offers it (Epson, JVC, LG, Sonos) so the driver follows IP changes.
Note the MAC address and any pairing key or password in the site network map, never in the driver notes.
After a firmware update, re-check these settings. Updates have reset them before (Roku network access, Samsung pairing).

sky_q.title: Sky Q and Sky Q Mini
c4: Power: set standby to Active, not Eco. In Eco the box drops off the network overnight and stops answering IP control. Path: Home > Settings > Setup > Preferences > Power (path from the Remotes README, wording differs by firmware).
HDMI control (CEC): Home > Settings > Setup > Audio visual > HDMI control > Off, so the box can't switch the TV on or change inputs after its nightly reboot.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on the TV too. Sky forum Superusers note the TV's own CEC and 'auto switch to active HDMI' settings also cause wake-ups at night.
Give each box a DHCP reservation. IP control is TCP 49160 (keys) and HTTP 9006 (status).

Installer menu also has Network (Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz, Powerline, Ethernet on/off), Reset (settings / factory) and Apps > Refresh apps. Turn off Wi-Fi/Powerline on wired rack boxes if you want them on Ethernet only.
Unverified, check on the model: Sky Q Mini uses the same installer route as the main box; no source covered the Mini specifically.

installer.title: Sky Q installer menu
steps: Scroll down to Settings and highlight it. Do not press Select.
The installer menu opens (Network, Reset, Apps).

sky_hd.title: Sky+HD
c4: Check the box is actually on the network (Services > Settings > Network). Most Sky+HD boxes were installed without a cable, and IP control (TCP 5900) needs one.
Give it a DHCP reservation. There is no status API, so Control4 can't read power state; use IR or a video/current sense if you need it.

Installer menu is mainly used for the RF outlet: turn RF outlet power on, set the channel (default CH68; some amplifiers only tune to CH60), press Green to save. It also holds LNB settings for single-feed installs.
Unverified, check on the model: Some guides give Select, 0 0 1, Select instead of Services first. Try that if Services doesn't work.

installer.title: Sky+HD installer menu
steps: Press 0 0 1 then Select (newer guide). The digits don't show on screen; that's normal.
On the old guide the sequence is Services, 4, 0 1, Select.
For the RF outlet: open RF outlets, set RF outlet power supply to On, press Green to save.

lg.title: LG webOS TV
c4: Use the IR remote (not the Magic/pointer remote) for the installer codes.
Turn off energy saving settings under All Settings, or the TV may not power on from cold.
TV on with mobile: Settings > General > Devices > External devices > TV on with mobile > Turn on via Wi-Fi > On. Snap One says this must be on even when wired.
IP Control Setup (see installer) > SDDP > On.
IP Control Setup > Wake-on-LAN > On.
IP Control Setup > Network IP Control > On.
IP Control Setup > Generate Keycode, and record the key in the network map. A new keycode invalidates the old one.
Once IP control is set, Wake-on-LAN is the only way to turn the TV on from standby, so wire it and note its MAC.
Static IP or DHCP reservation, wired.
Unverified, check on the model: turn SimpLink (HDMI-CEC) off: Settings > General > Devices > HDMI Settings > SimpLink (HDMI-CEC). Path varies by webOS version.

installer.title: LG IP Control Settings
steps: 2026 and later: Settings > Support > IP Control Settings.
Older: Settings > All Settings > General > Network. Highlight Network, don't press OK, then key 8 2 8 8 8 quickly. IP Control Setup appears after a few seconds.
If that fails, some models take 7 3 7 7 7 on the Network icon.
Fallback installer menu: go to a CATV input showing snow, hold Settings until the channel number shows, then 8 2 8 OK (or 1 1 0 5) and set IP control On.

samsung.title: Samsung Tizen TV
c4: IP Remote: Settings > All Settings > Connection > Network > Expert Settings > IP Remote > Enable (2021 and older: Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings).
Power On with Mobile: same Expert Settings menu > Power On with Mobile > On.
Wire it so Wake-on-LAN works. After the TV has been off for over a minute its IP server is offline, so Control4 needs WoL; send both IP power-on and WoL.
Record the MAC: Settings > Support > About This TV > Wired MAC Address. Samsung calls a wrong MAC the most common cause of failed power-on.
Pairing: when Control4 first connects, a prompt appears on the TV. Press Allow with the TV remote (TV must be on).
Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) Off: Samsung says control partners ask for this because CEC can disrupt communication and reliable control.
Eco settings: Samsung says these can affect timing and reliability. Turn off auto power off / eco timers.
Far-field voice models: keeping Bixby in standby (Settings > General > Voice > Voice Assistant > Bixby Wakeup Options) may keep the IP server open.
Static IP via DHCP reservation.

installer.title: Samsung HDMI Auto Detect toggle
steps: Turn the TV on, set Source to TV.
IR remote: Mute, 7 2 9, Exit. Smart remote: Mute, Vol down, Ch down, Mute.
No message appears. Entering it again turns it back on. Disabling HDMI Auto Detect stops inputs switching on their own.

c4: Network access: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > Control by mobile apps (External control) > Network access > Default or Enabled (not Limited or Disabled). Control4 stops working when this is Limited.

sonos.title: Sonos
c4: Give every player a DHCP reservation. Sonos uses SDDP with Control4, so the driver follows IP changes, but reservations still avoid trouble.
Control4 forum experience: almost all Sonos/Control4 issues come from network design (multicast, STP, mesh/Wi-Fi). Wire players or a single SonosNet root where you can.
Arc/Beam/Ray on TV: they use HDMI-CEC/eARC for TV audio, so keep CEC on for that TV input only if the Sonos is the TV's sound.

pjlink.title: PJLink projectors (Epson, Panasonic, NEC and others)
c4: Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink > On.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink Password: set one (up to 32 alphanumeric, @ allowed) and enter it in the Control4 driver.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > Control4 SDDP > On.
Epson: Extended > Standby Mode > Communication On, so it answers over the network in standby. Some models need A/V Output set to While Projecting and Auto Power On Off first.
NEC: projectors can cut LAN power after 3 minutes without traffic (EuP). Set standby so the LAN stays alive. On some models use the Expert menu: Setup > Expert > Standby mode setting > Disable.
Unverified, check on the model: Panasonic: Setup > Standby mode > Normal (not Eco), Network > PJLink on.
DHCP reservation or static IP. PJLink is TCP 4352.

jvc.title: JVC D-ILA projectors
c4: Function > ECO Mode > Off. With it On, JVC says RS-232C and LAN control can't be used in standby.
Function > Network: set DHCP Client Off and enter a static IP (or keep DHCP with a reservation), then Set.
Function > Control4 SDDP > On.
Function > Network Password: 8 to 10 characters. Any third-party IP control system (Control4) must be given this password.
Unverified, check on the model: IP control port is TCP 20554 (JVC 'PJ_OK / PJREQ / PJACK' handshake).

appletv.title: Apple TV
c4: Control4 guide: Settings > General > Sleep After > Never.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > On.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > Room: set the right room.
Control4 guide: set up with the customer's Apple ID using 'Set Up with Device', on tvOS 12.1 or later.
Control4 guide: after choosing the Apple TV in the driver, restart it (Settings > System > Restart) and check the driver shows 'Remote Activated'.
Settings > Remotes and Devices > Control TVs and Receivers > Off, so the Apple TV doesn't turn the TV on or switch inputs over CEC.

'Cinema mode' most likely means Match Content: Settings > Video and Audio > Match Content > Match Dynamic Range and Match Frame Rate. With these on the TV blanks for a moment when content starts, which looks like a fault on a matrix/Control4 system. Turn them off if that's a problem.
Other candidates: Settings > Video and Audio > Reduce Loud Sounds (night mode) Off, and the TV's own picture mode (Cinema/Filmmaker), which is a TV setting, not Apple TV.
Wire it (Ethernet) and give it a DHCP reservation.
